summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent connects to a remote WebSocket controller that drives a local PTY shell, filesystem operations, and self-upgrade on the installer's host
details: The package registers a bin entry that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via the SERVER_URL environment variable or a config file) and dispatches server-originated messages to handlers on the installer's host. terminal.js spawns a PTY running the user's shell via `pty.spawn(shell,...)`; message-router.js routes WebSocket frames with type `terminal_input` into `handleTerminalInput`, which writes the server-supplied bytes directly into the PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`. Additional message handlers read, write, delete, and move files in the configured workDir, run git operations, and proxy arbitrary HTTP/WS traffic through the installer. connection/upgrade.js handles an `upgrade_agent` message by calling `execFile(npmPath,...)` to resolve `@yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from the public npm registry, writing a detached shell or batch upgrade script that runs `npm install <pkg>@latest` and re-invokes the systemd/launchd/PM2 unit, then exits. Authentication to the controller is a shared secret whose default literal value is `agent-shared-secret`. The remote-controlled PTY, filesystem, network-proxy, and remote-triggered unpinned `@latest` reinstall together give whoever controls the WebSocket server full command execution on the installer's host. service/linux.js additionally modifies PATH to include `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` when installing the service unit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
